This closes a real gap (the route previously had neither gate, unlike its order-placement sibling) but has a side effect worth its own follow-up: cron.py (the automated exit path -- settlement-lag closes, model-reversal exits) already aborts its entire run under either gate, and main.py has no standalone CLI command to manually close an arbitrary open paper position (`undo` only reverses a just-placed trade within a short window, not a general close). With both the dashboard and cron now blocked and no CLI alternative, there is currently NO operator-facing way to close an open position at all while the kill switch or TRADING_PAUSED is engaged -- which matters specifically because closing a position is a risk-REDUCING action, the opposite of what a kill switch is meant to block. Not fixed as part of batch-41 (which only mirrored the existing sibling-route pattern per its own directive, correctly -- adding an operator override for the close path specifically is a separate design decision with its own tradeoffs, not a mechanical parity fix). Noted in LIVE_TRADING_RUNBOOK.md's kill- switch section as the batch-41 note under "Immediate halt (emergency)". What it would look like: either (a) a new `main.py close <trade_id> [exit_price]` CLI command that bypasses the two gates entirely (closing is not itself a live-order-placement action, so the same LiveTradingGate reasoning that blocks new orders doesn't obviously apply), or (b) carve /api/close- position's gate check out with its own justification (e.g. only block if manual=false and a live quote exists, since a kill-switch scenario is exactly when an operator might need to exit at a stale/manual price). Needs a real decision, not a default -- surface via AskUserQuestion when picked up. Source: opus review of audit/handoff_prompts/batches/batch-41.md's implementation, LOW-9.
